1.title: Run, Pup, Run!
1.topic: playing with a pet puppy in the sun (pets, animals, family)
lines: *Run*, | pup, | *run*! | Run in the *sun*.
Run *up* | the *hill*. | It is *fun*! ↘
*Sit*, | pup, | *sit*! | Sit on the *rug*.
*Wag*, | pup, | *wag*! | Can I *get* a *hug*? ↗
*Yes*! | Pup can *jump* | *up*!
*Hug*, | hug, | *hug*! | I *love* my *pup*! ↘
sounds: run, sun, pup, fun, rug, hug
입을 살짝 벌리고 힘을 빼고 짧게 '어' 해요. run은 '런', '룬'이 아니에요.
끝이 같은 단어는 운율(rhyme)이 맞아요. 앞소리만 바꿔 리듬 있게 읽어 보세요.
Can I ~? 질문은 끝을 올려요. 대답 Yes!는 힘차게 내려요.
1.expression: Clap a steady beat on each “Run, pup, run!”, sound hopeful on “Can I get a hug?” and give yourself a big hug at the end.

2.title: The Broken Crayon
2.topic: a red crayon snaps in half and a friend turns it into sharing (school, feelings, friendship)
lines: Mia *opened* | her new box | of *crayons*.
She *picked* the red one | and *pressed* too hard. | *Snap*!
The crayon *cracked* | in *half*! ↘
“Oh *no*,” | Mia *sighed*. | “My *best* color!”
Her friend Sam *looked* at the pieces | and *smiled*.
“Now you have *two* red crayons,” | he said. | “Can I *borrow* one?” ↗
Mia *laughed* | and *handed* him a piece.
Together they *colored* | a big red *fire truck*! ↘
sounds: k, s 뒤의 -ed는 짧은 t 소리예요. picked는 '픽트'처럼 한 박자로 끝내요.
모음이나 n, l, r 뒤의 -ed는 d 소리예요. smiled는 '스마일드' 한 박자예요.
t, d 뒤의 -ed만 '이드'로 한 박자가 더 생겨요: HAN-ded.
2.expression: Say “Snap!” sharply, sigh sadly on “Oh no,” then let Sam sound kind and playful when he asks to borrow one.

3.title: Why Do We Have Day and Night?
3.topic: Earth spinning makes day and night (science, space)
lines: Every morning, | the sun seems to *rise*. | Every evening, | it seems to *set*.
But the sun is not really *moving* | across the sky. ↘
*We* are the ones | who are moving! ↘
Earth *spins* | like a giant *top*. | It makes one full *turn* | every *day*.
When your side of Earth *faces* the sun, | it is *daytime*.
When your side *turns away* | from the sun, | it is *night*.
So while it is *day* in Korea, | it is *night* in New York!
We cannot *feel* Earth spinning, | because it turns so *smoothly*.
Try this: | shine a *lamp* | on a *ball* | and slowly *turn* the ball.
Can you see where it is *day* | and where it is *night*? ↗
sounds: igh는 '아이' 소리이고 gh는 소리가 나지 않아요. night는 '나잍'처럼 끝 t를 짧게 멈춰요.
혀끝을 윗니와 아랫니 사이에 살짝 내밀어요. Earth 끝은 바람만 나오는 th, smoothly는 목이 울리는 th예요.
But the sun is not really moving… WE are the ones who are moving!
생각을 뒤집을 때는 바뀐 말(We)을 크고 길게 강조해요.
3.expression: Ask the opening like a puzzle, say “We are the ones who are moving!” as a surprise, and read the experiment like a friendly science teacher.

4.title: The Night the Lights Went Out
4.topic: a storm knocks out the power and a family makes shadow animals by flashlight (family, feelings, weather)
lines: On a *windy* November night, | the lights in Hana's house | *flickered*— | and went *out*. ↘
The fridge stopped *humming*. | The TV went *silent*. | Everything was *dark*.
Hana *grabbed* her little brother's hand. | “I don't *like* this,” | Minu *whispered*.
Dad found a *flashlight* | in the kitchen drawer | and *clicked* it on.
“A *storm* knocked out the power,” | he said *calmly*. | “It will come *back* soon.”
Mom *lit* a *candle* | and set it on the table, | far away from the *curtains*.
Then Dad held up his hands | in front of the flashlight, | and a *rabbit* appeared | on the *wall*!
Minu *giggled*. | “Do a *dog*!” | he begged.
Soon everyone was making *shadow animals*— | a *bird*, | a *snail*, | and even a wobbly *elephant*.
Then Mom told a story | about the night *she* lost power | when she was a girl in *Busan*.
Hana *forgot* to be scared. | She even forgot | about the *TV*.
Suddenly, | the lights *flashed* back on, | and the fridge began to *hum*. ↘
Everyone *blinked* | in the bright light.
“*Aww*,” | said Minu. | “Can we turn them *off* again?” ↗
sounds: “I don't like this,” (scared whisper), “It will come back soon.” (calm), “Do a dog!” (excited)
해설은 이야기하듯, 미누는 처음엔 작게 속삭이다가 점점 신나게, 아빠는 낮고 차분하게 읽어요.
calmly의 l은 소리가 나지 않아요. '캄리'처럼 읽고, '칼믈리'로 읽지 마요.
f·b와 l 사이에 '으'를 넣지 마요. '플-'이 아니라 입술과 혀를 한 번에 붙여 fl을 빠르게 이어요.
4.expression: Start slow and spooky as the lights go out, let the middle grow warm and playful with the shadow animals, and end with Minu's disappointed “Aww.”
events: On a windy November night, the lights in Hana's house went out.
Hana held her little brother Minu's hand because he was scared of the dark.
Dad found a flashlight and calmly said a storm had knocked out the power.
Mom lit a candle and set it far away from the curtains.
Dad made a shadow rabbit on the wall, and Minu giggled.
Everyone made shadow animals, and Mom told a story about losing power in Busan.
Hana forgot to be scared, and the lights suddenly came back on.
Minu was sad and asked if they could turn the lights off again.
